pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:69 The judge/candidate pin for the default spec (`opus@xhigh`) goes through a first-party tier-alias roster (`opus` -> an undated id), so a routine roster edit silently swaps the instrument; judge-stability calls this case out by name, and stamping the response's `model` only partly mitigates it.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:69 Tier aliases resolve through a local roster table to undated ids instead of being pinned to a concrete dated identifier. Mitigations exist but do not close the gap: the response's `model` is stamped (anthropic_api.rs:213), and own-family preference is controlled by same_family (family.rs:30).

crates/engine/src/lib.rs:347 An unparseable judge sample is dropped rather than scored zero, and all-failed returns an error rather than a phantom zero, so error stays a separate verdict. Deterministic scorers are reported as model "deterministic".

crates/engine/src/pool.rs:12 Fan-out goes through a bounded worker pool with declared `jobs`, and results come back in index order rather than completion order. Retry is bounded by MAX_TRIES and CALL_BUDGET in retry.rs. The provider_boundary test drives the real path against a loopback stub.
